The complete June30 primary petition, not February22 Paul and not the following Peter commemoration, is read in all three witnesses. Both older witnesses actually print natalitia;1962 prints natalicia. The exact accepted same-word pair is neuter accusative plural, the direct object of colimus in both full contexts. No commemorationem is substituted. Printed1962 cuius/eius are represented by established calendar cujus/ejus. Pustet omits the target comma after ut; Mame prints a colon after quaesumus where target has a semicolon. Pustet actually ends Per Dominum.; Mame actually ends only Per.; the1962 Paul paragraph has no conclusion or cue and ends sentiamus. It is followed by Et fit commemoratio S.Petri Ap.sub unica conclusione and a distinct Peter Oratio2924. Neither historical cue nor Peter ending is supplied to Paul.

Every complete primary June30 Perceptis petition word agrees in target, Pustet and Mame. This is not the February22 Sanctificati prayer. Pustet has a comma after sacramentis rather than target colon, colon after deprecamur rather than target semicolon, and lacks target comma after ut. Mame agrees in target petition pointing. Pustet actually ends Per Dominum.; Mame prints Per followed by its visibly contracted Dnum/Dñum form, not an editorially expanded Dominum. The1962 Paul paragraph has no conclusion or cue and ends medelam.; the separately headed Pro S.Petro Postcommunio2936 owns the following ending. No Peter ending or old cue is copied into this body.

It is neither an edition of a historical hand missal nor an edition of the Missale Romanum. Each artifact records the transformation rule over separate public-domain antecedent and 1962 page-image witnesses; its passages let consumers cite the projected bodies without assigning Triptych's target-controlled collation choices to the antecedent printing.
